entities.name: Janusz Suchywilk
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Janusz Suchywilk of Grzymala Coat of Arms (died 1382), Archbishop of Gniezno and Primate of Poland, served as a pivotal statesman and ecclesiastical leader during a tumultuous period in Polish history, bridging the end of the Piast dynasty and the ascent of the Anjou rulers. As Chancellor of the Crown under King Casimir III the Great, he wielded significant political influence, contributing to the codification of Polish law and the stabilization of the kingdom's internal affairs. His familial ties to Jarosław z Bogorii i Skotnik, a prominent statesman and archbishop, further solidified his position within the Polish elite and the Church hierarchy, positioning him as a crucial figure in both secular administration and spiritual leadership.

Suchywilk’s career trajectory saw him rise from a canon in Gniezno and Kraków to the esteemed position of Chancellor in 1357, a role he maintained until 1373. During this time, he was instrumental in implementing Casimir III's legal reforms, particularly contributing to the statutes of Wiślica and Piotrków, which unified the diverse legal traditions of Greater and Lesser Poland. Upon Casimir III's death in 1370, Suchywilk played a critical role in the succession, initially supporting Casimir's grandson, Casimir IV, Duke of Słupsk, before eventually acquiescing to the ascension of Louis I of Hungary, as stipulated by earlier agreements. His election as Archbishop of Gniezno in 1374 solidified his spiritual authority, allowing him to navigate the complex political landscape as an arbiter between the Polish nobility and the new Hungarian monarch.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Janusz Suchywilk's strategic leadership as Primate and Chancellor was crucial in stabilizing Poland during a fraught dynastic transition, preventing wider conflict and preserving the kingdom's legal and ecclesiastical structures for future generations, ultimately influencing the shape of the Jagiellonian era.
